Changes and the indicator index

Source: vignettes/tables.Rmd
tables.Rmd

The Change (%) tab of the golemworldbank app lists the indicators that rose and fell for a country between two years, and the Index tab lists every indicator with its definition. In R, indicator_change() makes the comparison, render_change_table() shows its tables and render_index_table() shows the index. The tables are DT tables, which can be searched and sorted.

library(golemworldbank)

What changed between two years

indicator_change() compares every indicator that a country has a value for in both years. The percent change is (value2 - value1) / |value1| * 100, the change relative to the value of the first year:

res <- indicator_change(mfi_table(), country = "Greece", year1 = 2000, year2 = 2020)
nrow(res$increased)
#> [1] 388
nrow(res$decreased)
#> [1] 368

res$increased and res$decreased have a row per indicator, with its values in the two years, the change and the percent change, the largest change first. Indicators that did not change are in neither. When the country has no data in either year, indicator_change() stops with an error.

Some indicators are left out of both, because their percent change says little:

  • The rates of change, such as “GDP growth (annual %)” or “Inflation, consumer prices (annual %)”, whose names contain “annual %”, “% change” or “growth”. A percent change of a growth rate means little. include_rates = TRUE keeps them.
  • The indicators whose value changed sign, such as net inflows that went from -8 million to +6.7 billion, which would read as +82,000%. include_sign_change = TRUE keeps them, and res$sign_change lists them either way.
  • The indicators whose value was 0 in the first year, where the percent change is not defined. res$zero_base lists them.
writeLines(res$sign_change)
#> Discrepancy in expenditure estimate of GDP (current LCU)
#> Foreign direct investment, net (BoP, current US$)
#> Foreign direct investment, net inflows (% of GDP)
#> Foreign direct investment, net inflows (BoP, current US$)
#> Net errors and omissions (BoP, current US$)
#> Portfolio equity, net inflows (BoP, current US$)
#> Portfolio investment, net (BoP, current US$)
writeLines(res$zero_base)
#> Cause of death, by other COVID-19 pandemic-related outcomes (% of total)
#> Discrepancy in expenditure estimate of GDP (constant LCU)
#> Electricity production from nuclear sources (% of total)

For an indicator that is itself a percentage, such as “Urban population (% of total population)”, the percent change is relative to the old percentage. It is not the difference in percentage points, which is the Change column.

Change tables

render_change_table() shows one of the two tables. The values and the change are shown to 3 significant digits, such as 6.02M, while sorting still uses the full numbers. The percent change is in bold, green for an increase and red for a decrease. The tables are long, so here they show only their first 10 rows, the largest changes:

render_change_table(head(res$increased, 10))
render_change_table(head(res$decreased, 10))

render_change_table(res$increased) shows the whole table on one long page, as the app does.

The indicator index

render_index_table() lists the indicators of the data you give it, in the order they first appear there, with their World Bank topic and definition from indicator_info. The Index tab gives it the whole of mfi_table(), which lists all 1,497 indicators on one long page:

render_index_table(mfi_table(), indicator_info)

Here it gets only the rows of the indicators whose names start with “GDP per capita”:

per_capita <- subset(mfi_table(), startsWith(`Indicator Name`, "GDP per capita"))
render_index_table(per_capita, indicator_info)

Save a table

htmlwidgets::saveWidget() saves any of the tables as a web page:

htmlwidgets::saveWidget(render_change_table(res$increased), "increased.html")
